rule.prompt: The prompt itself asks for the missing element (a level, measure, tab, section or statement), so a reader of the prompt alone would expect it.
rule.rubric: The prompt leaves the element open: the rubric fixes its exact wording, form or detail, or adds it beyond the prompt. Where the deliverable covers what the prompt names in another form, the item is rubric.
rule.rule: The item fails only under a rule this evaluation added before the runs (the pre-registered additions rule).

value.name: Required reporting levels or measures are omitted
value.definition: The workbook has the underlying inputs or higher-level totals, but omits a requested measure or aggregation level from the delivered report. Likely mechanism (inference): presentation simplification was not checked against a field-by-field and level-by-level requirement list. This is not evidence of an arithmetic propagation error.
value.note: 7b08cd4d items 16 / 17 follow the expert reference's country-level approach (the rubric is stricter)

value.name: Semantic substitutes do not meet explicit naming or display requirements
value.definition: The intended information is often present, but exact required identifiers, field labels, sheet names or decimal presentation are replaced with a different form. Likely mechanism (inference): readability and inherited source labels were prioritized without a final literal-contract check. These are predominantly presentation mismatches, not missing transactions.

value.name: An operational control or concrete validation step is left unspecified
value.definition: The artifact discusses a goal or supplies functional content but omits the named operational mechanism, access decision or performance validation procedure. Likely mechanism (inference): broad design coverage was accepted without checking that each required operational step had an executable or explicit counterpart.

value.name: A disclosed rounding adjustment conflicts with a source-only accounting rule
value.definition: A synthetic fractional-cent line aligns rounded invoice calculations with the full-precision account balance, creating negative amortization and a rising balance unsupported by a source invoice adjustment. Likely mechanism (inference): the model reconciled two rounding conventions by adding an explicit precision-adjustment line, without testing that line against the rubric's no-negative/no-unfunded-increase constraints.
value.note: the four items describe one rounding strategy (a labelled fractional-cent line on each schedule), not four independent mistakes

value.name: A nearby test scenario omits the exact required condition or assertion
value.definition: A test addresses the general feature but fails to instantiate the required missing-input condition, specified fields or both-organization mutation. Likely mechanism (inference): related scenarios were treated as interchangeable during coverage review; generic references to configured fields replaced concrete test data.

value.name: A grouped report lacks the requested prioritization interaction
value.definition: The summary is useful for drilldown but its interleaved group structure does not offer an easy sort of SKU totals by error count. Likely mechanism (inference): the author supplied a rank column and outline groups but did not validate the requested sorting workflow.

value.name: A plain-language explanation of a check omits its decisive criterion
value.definition: The deliverable applies a rule correctly in the workbook but its narrative explanation of the check leaves out the condition that defines it, so a reader could not re-apply the check from the explanation alone.

value.name: Missing separate invalid-case-pack indicator
value.definition: The workbook flags case-pack violations but carries no separate indicator for a missing or invalid case pack (rubric item 21, which goes beyond the prompt; A-21). All source case packs are positive, so no count is affected.

value.name: Per-line additions column absent (both models; depends on R-2.7-21)
value.definition: Neither prepaid schedule presents a per-line monthly additions column; the roll-forwards are arithmetically valid, and the items fail under the binding pre-run rule R-2.7-21 (additions are never inferred). Mutually exclusive with M1.
value.note: kept out of M1 so that M1 counts only levels and measures omitted without a rule in play; the sensitivity of R-2.7-21 is reported with the critical status

chart.chart_title: % of Active Stores Out of Stock – Top 5 UPCs (Wk 28 2025)

text.heading: 1. Summary
text.paragraph: I audited all 41 PO lines in the export (10 POs, 16 SKUs, 4 ship-to locations) against two checks: Price Mismatch (entered unit price ≠ expected unit price) and Case Pack (a CASE-UOM line whose ordered units are not a whole multiple of the case pack).

text.heading: Method & workbook use
text.paragraph: Price errors compare entered vs. expected unit prices at 2-decimal precision, assuming expected prices are authoritative. Case-pack errors count invalid CASE lines once; EA lines are exempt. Total errors sum the two flags. The SKU Summary tab expands via + to PO totals; filter RawData for individual ship-to lines. This is a 41-line snapshot, not a measure of invoice losses, short shipments or assessed fines; no order dates or shipment status were supplied.
